headline: Computational profiling of SARS-CoV-2 and influenza A variation and host adaptation
label: Respiratory Virus Variant Analysis
summary: Recent 2026 preprints and publications pair machine learning and web tools with respiratory virus variant, antigenic, and host-adaptation data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational analysis of respiratory virus variation, applied to variant classification, antigenic analysis, host adaptation, and diagnostic assay design. Most items concern SARS-CoV-2 or influenza A. One preprint converts direct coupling analysis of epistatic mutations into Circos images and classifies Alpha, Delta, Omicron, and other variants with convolutional neural networks; this Circos-based encoding of epistatic coupling for CNN classification is the new methodological element. FluNexus, also a preprint, preprocesses HA1 and HI data for H1, H3, and H5 and provides online antigenic prediction with manifold-based antigenic cartography. A published study reports that IFITM3 deficiency drives SARS-CoV-2 adaptation across animal species while preserving variant-specific traits. RAZOR catalogs PCR primers targeting human respiratory viruses. A separate preprint, CEI, addresses T-cell receptor clonal expansion after SARS-CoV-2 vaccination, a more immunological scope than the remaining items.
